proposal.summary: Customer Service (SH-CS) requested an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and auto-fix wrong bills, framing the doubling of dispute volume since August (610→1260/month, E-05) as a response-capacity problem (CL-01). Investigation found this framing is contradicted: response times are already within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d target, E-03), and 59% of disputed bills are on correctly-read ACTUAL meters (E-02), not estimates — ruling out field staffing shortfalls (E-07, E-09, E-10) and tariff changes (E-04, E-06) as primary causes, and pointing instead to a billing import/validation defect, plausibly a rule change around August (H-RULE-CHANGE-ERROR, supported by E-02, E-04, E-06, E-12). The release delivered the two completed, read-only analysis work items (disputed-bills-by-read-type on DA-BILL, field-route-completion review on DA-ROUTE; W-WI-BILL-ANALYZE, W-WI-ROUTE-REVIEW) and decided RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION rather than a full fix, because the critical confirming step — querying the billing-config rule-change log (DA-RULES) to verify the August rule change — remains open (VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED) and falls outside this release's scope. No automated bill writes or dispatch changes were made, consistent with K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH authority constraints.
key_points: Problem as defined (PD-1): dispute tickets roughly doubled since August 2026 (610 to 1260/month, E-05), and 59% of disputed bills are on ACTUAL (correctly read) meters versus 41% ESTIMATED (E-02), indicating a billing-side calculation defect rather than estimate substitution or response-capacity issues.

The requester's framing (CL-01: root cause is response capacity, requested an auto-answer/auto-fix AI agent) is CONTRADICTED by evidence: dispute response times are within the 3.0-day SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d, E-03), so Customer Service is not overwhelmed.

Field reader staffing shortfall (CL-03/E-07, a stakeholder claim) and route completion shortfall (88% vs 95% target, E-01) were established as real but secondary: they affect only 320 estimated accounts (E-09) and 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes, not the majority 1785 ACTUAL-read disputes (E-02).
Tariff change was ruled out: billing-db tariff change log has zero records (E-04), corroborated by SH-BILL's statement (E-06).

For disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, 1184 of 1240 had valid AMI reads received but were REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION during billing import (E-12), pointing to a billing-import validation rule issue rather than AMI feed failure or field shortfall.

Leading hypothesis H-RULE-CHANGE-ERROR (a billing import validation rule change around August causing calculation errors) is SUPPORTED by E-02, E-04, E-06, E-12, but not yet confirmed because the billing-config rule-change log itself (DA-RULES) has not been queried (assumption A-RULE-CHANGE-TIMING; unknown/VOB U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED remains OPEN).

What was released: two completed, read-only analysis work items — analyze_disputed_bills_by_read_type on DA-BILL and review_field_route_completion on DA-ROUTE (W-WI-BILL-ANALYZE, W-WI-ROUTE-REVIEW, both DONE) — matching the release scope in solution_design SD-1; no bill writes or dispatch changes were executed, consistent with K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH.

Decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION. The DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, with the critical confirming step (querying DA-RULES to verify the rule change) deferred as VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED, which is open and outside this release's scope — this is why the diagnosis is released as supported-but-unconfirmed rather than a completed root-cause fix.
limitations_explained: The core hypothesis (billing import rule change) is not yet confirmed: VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED is OPEN and the billing-config rule-change log has not been queried; its blocking scope lies outside this release.
Response SLA is already within target and is not the mechanism driving the dispute surge, so no response-time optimization was undertaken or is in scope.
Handoffs H-FIELD-BILL and H-MDMS-BILL have UNKNOWN delivery_status and semantic_validity per gate findings, which could affect the accuracy of the DA-BILL read-type data underlying this analysis.

AMI feed access via DA-MDMS remains blocked (VOB-U-AMI-FEED-ACCESS; mdms-export tool health DEGRADED/HOLD, status NOT_TRANSIENT), limiting direct verification of AMI read event data beyond what E-12 already captured.

Manual rebilling of the roughly 1785 disputed ACTUAL-read accounts (remedy SR-R-REBILL-AFFECTED) is unlikely to complete within the contest time window and requires Billing Operations (K-BILLWRITE) sign-off, which has not occurred.
Negotiating field staffing changes (remedy SR-R-FIELD-STAFFING-SECONDARY) only addresses the minority ESTIMATED-read dispute driver and exceeds the contest time budget; it was not pursued.
The underlying root cause has not been remediated (no rule revert/fix, SR-R-REVERT-FIX-RULE, has occurred) — this release delivers diagnostic analysis only, not a corrective action.
